critical_code_review_comments: leads_router.list_leads: normalizes ALL leads (all_normalized) just to compute verified_count/ready_count, then throws them away and returns only the paginated slice. For large runs (500+ leads) this is O(n) work on every page request. Consider caching those counters on lead_results or computing at callback time.

leads_router._normalize_lead composite id `${request_id}-${index}` is positional; if a callback overwrites row.leads with a reordered list, existing composite ids in the UI become stale and send-to-outreach may target the wrong lead. Consider a stable uuid per lead at insert time.

leads_router.send_to_outreach: mutates row.leads with a Python list then does update(...).values(leads=leads_list) - JSON column update fine, but there is no row-lock so two concurrent send-to-outreach on the same run can lose an update. Consider SELECT FOR UPDATE or increment counters instead of full-array rewrite.
meetings_router.parse_dt: `datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace('Z','+00:00'))` will raise ValueError with a 500 for malformed input from the UI (e.g. '2026-03-15T'); wrap in try/except -> 400.
